== Biography ==

Anne was born on 11 March 1788. She was the natural daughter of [[Glasgow-1076|Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan]] and Annie Swann. On 2 August 1804 in Edinburgh, Midlothian, Anne married [[Robertson-30564|Robert Robertson]]. They had ten children. Anne passed away in France on 29 July 1867.<ref>Find a Grave, database and images (https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/153319836/anne-robertson: accessed May 18, 2026), memorial page for Anne Glasgow Robertson (11 Mar 1788–29 Jul 1867), Find a Grave Memorial ID 153319836, citing Kilwinning Churchyard, Kilwinning, North Ayrshire, Scotland; Maintained by Pixturmn (contributor 47729036).</ref>

Spouses.Name: Robertson-30564
Spouses.bio:
{{Notables Sticker}}

=== Biography ===
=== Robert Glasgow (late Robertson) ===

'''Profile & Legacies Summary'''
*1775 - 27th Jan 1845*Robert Robertson, later known as Robert Glasgow, was the eldest son of Alexander Robertson of Gunsgreen House, Eyemouth. Initially titled "Esquire of Prenderguest," Robert was later designated "Esquire of Montgreenan" after inheriting the estates of his father-in-law, Dr. Robert Glasgow, in 1828<ref name="T71-892">T71/892, Counterclaim from Robert Glasgow Esq. and Anne his wife, withdrawn.</ref>. This inheritance included the Montgreenan estate in Ayrshire, Scotland, and the Mont Greenan and Sans Souci sugar plantations in St. Vincent<ref name="T71-1266">T71/1266, Marriage of Robert Robertson of Prenderguest to Anne Glasgow.</ref>. As per Dr. Glasgow's will, Robert changed his surname from Robertson to Glasgow<ref>Will of Robert Glasgow, 14/10/1828, Edinburgh Sheriff Court papers SC 6/44/4/1.</ref>.

==== Education and Professional Life ====
Robert Robertson graduated in Medicine from the University of Edinburgh in 1797 and became a Fellow of the Royal College of Surgeons in 1802<ref>List of the Graduates in Medicine in the University of Edinburgh from MDCCV to MDCCCLXVI (Edinburgh, Neil & Co., 1867).</ref>. Despite his professional background as a physician, his wealth and prominence derived primarily from the Glasgow family estates and plantations.

==== Marriage and Family ====
In 1804, Robert married Anne Glasgow, the illegitimate daughter and sole heir of Dr. Robert Glasgow<ref name="T71-1266"/>. Together, they had four children:
* '''Robert (1811-1860):''' Heir, a J.P. and advocate<ref name=RobertGrave>{{FindAGrave | 146731548 | sameas=no }}.</ref>.
* '''Philadelphia Jane.'''
* '''Anne.'''
* '''Charlotte Marie Cecilia (born 1827 in Rome):''' Charlotte’s baptism was recorded in Edinburgh on 20/07/1828<ref>GROS OPR Births 685/1 560 78.</ref>.

In 1841, Robert Glasgow was living at Holly Walk, Leamington Priors, with family members and several servants. His wife, Anne, was not listed in the census.<ref>1841 census online.</ref> Robert Glasgow died at Pau, France, in 1845, leaving behind an estate valued at £5,141, with arrears of £4,081 due from his father-in-law’s estate.<ref>Email from Dr. Anthony J Cooke (09/02/2011).</ref>.

==== Estates and Legacy ====
After inheriting Montgreenan and Sans Souci in 1828, Robert submitted claims for compensation under the Slave Compensation Act following the abolition of slavery in the British Empire. He was awarded:
* '''£6,987 4s 0d for Mont Greenan''' in St. Vincent<ref name="T71-892"/>
* '''£6,418 15s 6d for Sans Souci''' in St. Vincent<ref name="T71-1266"/>

==== Post-Abolition Challenges ====
Robert Glasgow, like many plantation owners, struggled to maintain profitability after the abolition of slavery. The Sans Souci estate had to diversify from sugar to crops like cocoa and bananas, although labor shortages persisted<ref>Anthony Cooke, 'An elite revisited: Glasgow West India merchants, 1783-1877', Journal of Scottish Historical Studies 32.2 2012 pp. 127-165.</ref>.
=== Further Information ===
* '''Absentee:''' Yes  
* '''British/Irish:''' Yes  
* '''Name in Compensation Records:''' Robert Robertson

==== Spouse ====
* Anne Glasgow

==== Children ====
* Anne (1805-)
* Robert (1811-1860)<ref name=RobertGrave/>
* Philadelphia Jane
* Charlotte Marie Cecilia (1827-)

==== Occupation ====
* Physician, plantation owner, landowner

==== Associated Claims ====
* '''St Vincent 466 (Mont Greenan):''' £6,987 4s 0d<ref name="T71-892"/>
* '''St Vincent 481A-C (Sans Souci):''' £6,418 15s 6d<ref name="T71-1266"/>

==== Relationships ====
* '''Husband → Wife:''' Anne Glasgow late Robertson (née Glasgow)
* '''Son-in-law → Father-in-law:''' Dr. Robert Glasgow
* '''Brother:''' George Home Robertson

==== Estates ====
* '''Montgreenan Estate:''' Ayrshire, Scotland. Inherited from Dr. Robert Glasgow in 1828.
* '''Sans Souci Estate:''' St. Vincent. Inherited in 1828, facing economic decline post-abolition.
* '''Gunsgreen House:''' Eyemouth, Berwickshire, Scotland. Inherited in 1804 from his father, Alexander Robertson.

43931603.Name: Glasgow-2952
43931603.DeathLocation: Calliaqua, Saint George, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
43931603.bio:
== Biography == John was born about 1780. He was the natural son of [[Glasgow-1076|Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan]]. John Glasgow died at some point before September 1817; he appears to have owned a metalwork business, owning five blacksmiths, two coppersmiths, a carpenter, four labourers as well as three female house servants and five children. By 1822, two of the women and all five of the children had been purchased by the Montgreenan plantation. John's "housekeeper" (and common-law wife?), [[Theobalds-120|Amelia]], inherited enslaved people from John Glasgow for the term of her natural life: in March 1817 she registered ownership of Mary, age 25, a house servant and four children Adam (age 7), Eve (age 5), Peter (age 3), and James (age 1). Adam and his siblings may have the children of John and Amelia. == Reseach Notes == * [[Glasgow-1076|Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan]] had at least three natural children. A trust deed of 1803 reads as follows:
To my reputed natural mulatto son John and the lawful heirs of his body, I leave the sum of two hundred pounds sterling. To my reputed natural daughter Emilia and the lawful heirs of her body, I leave the sum of five hundred pounds sterling. To Robert, the reputed natural son of my late brother James and the lawful heirs etc... I leave the lawful sum of one hundred pounds sterling. To James the reputed natural son of my said brother etc.... the sum of fifty pounds sterling.
* Robert bequeathed the estates of Montgreenan and Sans Souci in St Vincent to his youngest natural daughter Anne and her husband Robert Robertson of Gunsgreen House, Eyemouth (both q.v.). The legacy was made conditional upon Robert assuming the name Glasgow. == Sources ==

Spouses.Name: Theobalds-120
Spouses.DeathLocation: Calliaqua, Saint George, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
Spouses.bio:
== Biography ==

Amelia is of uncertain identity, but she appears to have been the common-law wife of [[Glasgow-2952|John Glasgow]]. In his testament, John nominated Amelia Glasgow, his "housekeeper," as a beneficiary for the term of her natural life, and Amelia Glasgow was listed as a Proprietor in the Triennial Return of Slaves of 1827<ref>The National Archives of the UK; Kew, Surrey, England; Office of Registry of Colonial Slaves and Slave Compensation Commission: Records; Class: T 71; Piece Number: 498, p.246.</ref> and 1830.<ref>The National Archives of the UK; Kew, Surrey, England; Office of Registry of Colonial Slaves and Slave Compensation Commission: Records; Class: T 71; Piece Number: 499, p.221.</ref> She appears to have married not long after this time, as Amelia Theobalds was then listed in the Registry of Slaves in 1834.<ref>The National Archives of the UK; Kew, Surrey, England; Office of Registry of Colonial Slaves and Slave Compensation Commission: Records; Class: T 71; Piece Number: 500, p.280.</ref><ref>The National Archives of the UK; Kew, Surrey, England; Office of Registry of Colonial Slaves and Slave Compensation Commission: Records; Class: T 71; Piece Number: 500, p.349.</ref> She passed away about 1839.

== Research Notes ==
*The Slave Registers for St Vincent lists an enslaved girl given as Mina or Minna born c. 1828 and registered by Amelia Glasgow in 1828 and by Amelia Theobalds in 1834.<ref>https://www.ucl.ac.uk/lbs/person/view/2146662589</ref>
*This profile was previously erroneously connected as the daughter of [[Glasgow-1076|Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan]].

== Biography == 

{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}
Amelia was born about 1781 on the island of Saint Vincent, in what was then the British West Indies. She was the natural daughter of [[Glasgow-1076|Dr. Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan]] and [[Laborde-346|Rosalie Laborde]], who was of African descent. In 1803, her father executed a trust deed bequeathing several legacies, including "to my reputed natural daughter Emilia... £500."<ref>https://www.ucl.ac.uk/lbs/person/view/2146643739</ref> It appears by this time Amelia had moved to Kilbirnie, Ayrshire, Scotland, where her father was born and, on 17 December 1804 at Kilbirnie, she married [[Wilson-134817|Andrew Wilson of Wallace]].<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Banns and Marriages," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : viewed 30 Dec 2025), marriage of Andrew Wilson and Amelia Glasgow, 17 Dec 1804; citing Ref No: 10 / 248, parish 596: Andrew Wilson in Wallast and Amelia Glasgow in Bridge.</ref> They had at least five children:
#[[Wilson-135256|Jean Wilson]].<ref>Paisley High Church, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : accessed 30 Dec 2025), Jean Wilson 22 Dec 1808, daughter of Andrew and Emilia Glasgow; citing Ref 10 / 459, parish 573 / 1.</ref>
#[[Wilson-135257|Margaret Wilson]].<ref>Paisley High Church, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : accessed 30 Dec 2025), Margaret Wilson 28 Jun 1810, daughter of Andrew and Amelia Glasgow; citing Ref 10 / 477, parish 573 / 1.</ref>
#[[Wilson-135258|John Wilson]].<ref>Paisley High Church, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : accessed 30 Dec 2025), John Wilson 6 Aug 1812, son of Andrew and Amelia Glasgow; citing Ref 10 / 503, parish 573 / 1.</ref>
#[[Wilson-135259|Amelia Wilson]].<ref>Paisley High Church, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : accessed 30 Dec 2025), Amelia Wilson 2 Oct 1814, daughter of Andrew and Amelia Glasgow; citing Ref 10 / 529, parish 573 / 1.</ref>
#[[Wilson-135260|Robert Glasgow Wilson]].<ref>Paisley High Church, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : accessed 30 Dec 2025), Robert Glasgow Wilson 17 Jul 1817, son of Andrew and Amelia Glasgow; citing Ref 10 / 562, parish 573 / 1.</ref>
Following their marriage, Amelia and Andrew moved to Paisley, Renfrewshire, where their children were born and Andrew conducted business as a Merchant. In his last will and testament, Amelia's brother, John Glasgow, who passed away in or before 1817, nominated Amelia and her children as the primary beneficiaries to the profits of the sale of the enslaved men in his copper-smithing business in Kingstown, Saint Vincent.<ref>https://www.ucl.ac.uk/lbs/person/view/2146662589</ref> 

Amelia and her family later moved to Ardrossan, Ayrshire, where Andrew passed away on 31 August 1830.<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Death and Burials," database with images, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : viewed 30 Dec 2025), death of Andrew Wilson, 31 Aug 1830; citing Ref No: 20 / 282, parish 596: 31 Aug 1830 Died at Ardrossan Andrew Wilson portioner of Wallast in this parish.</ref> Amelia continued in Ardrossan for many years, in 1841 living next door to,<ref>"Scottish Census Returns - 1841" database with images, National Records of Scotland, ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : viewed 30 Dec 2025); citing Reference Number: 576 / 3 / 19: Emelia Wilson. Head. Age: 60. Occ: Independent. Birthplace: Scotland.</ref> and later with, her daughter Jean there.<ref>"Scottish Census Returns - 1851" database with images, National Records of Scotland, ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : viewed 30 Dec 2025); citing Reference Number: 576 / 11 / 14: Emelia Wilson. Head. Widow. Age: 70. Occ: Annuitant. Birthplace: St Vincent, West Indies; Jane Adam. Daughter. Widow. Age: 42. Occ: Proprietor. Birthplace: Paisley, Renfrewshire.</ref><ref>"Scottish Census Returns - 1861" database with images, National Records of Scotland, ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : viewed 30 Dec 2025); citing Reference Number: 576 /2 1 / 5: Emelia Wilson. Head. Widow. Age: 79. Occ: Annuitant. Birthplace: West Indies; Jane Adam. Daughter. Widow. Age: 42. Occ: Land & House Proprietor. Birthplace: Paisley, Renfrewshire.</ref> She passed away in Ardrossan on 23 September 1867.<ref>Scotland, "Statutory Registers - Deaths" database, National Records of Scotland, ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : viewed 30 Dec 2025) Amelia Wilson or Glasgow, F, age 87, mother's MS L'Aborde, 1867, Ardrossan New; citing Reference Number: 576 / 2 / 47: Amelia Wilson, widow of Andrew Wilson, Land Proprietor. Died 23 Sep 1867 at 45 Glasgow St., Ardrossan. Aged 87. Daughter of Robert Glasgow Surgeon (West Indies) (deceased) and Roselie Glasgow MS L'Aborde (deceased). COD: Old Age, as certified by James Stevens, surgeon. Informant: Maggie Shears, Dress Maker, present. Registered 28 September 1867.</ref> 

== Research Notes ==
Amelia is not to be confused with Amelia, the Housekeeper and (probably) common-law wife of her brother, [[Glasgow-2952|John Glasgow]], who continued to reside in Saint Vincent following John's death and was later known as [[Theobalds-120|Amelia Theobalds]].

== Biography ==

Andrew was baptised in Kilbirnie, Ayrshire, Scotland, on 11 October 1772.<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : accessed 30 Dec 2025), Andrew Wilson 11 Oct 1772, son of John Wilson and Jean Semple; citing Ref 10 / 178, parish 596.</ref> He was the son of [[Wilson-134790|John Wilson]] and [[Sempill-222|Jean Sempill]]. On 17 December 1804 at Kilbirnie, Andrew married [[Glasgow-3789|Amelia Glasgow]], natural daughter of Dr. Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan.<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Banns and Marriages," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : viewed 30 Dec 2025), marriage of Andrew Wilson and Amelia Glasgow, 17 Dec 1804; citing Ref No: 10 / 248, parish 596: Andrew Wilson in Wallast and Amelia Glasgow in Bridge.</ref> They had at least five children:
#[[Wilson-135256|Jean Wilson]].<ref>Paisley High Church, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : accessed 30 Dec 2025), Jean Wilson 22 Dec 1808, daughter of Andrew and Emilia Glasgow; citing Ref 10 / 459, parish 573 / 1.</ref>
#[[Wilson-135257|Margaret Wilson]].<ref>Paisley High Church, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : accessed 30 Dec 2025), Margaret Wilson 28 Jun 1810, daughter of Andrew and Amelia Glasgow; citing Ref 10 / 477, parish 573 / 1.</ref>
#[[Wilson-135258|John Wilson]].<ref>Paisley High Church, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : accessed 30 Dec 2025), John Wilson 6 Aug 1812, son of Andrew and Amelia Glasgow; citing Ref 10 / 503, parish 573 / 1.</ref>
#[[Wilson-135259|Amelia Wilson]].<ref>Paisley High Church, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : accessed 30 Dec 2025), Amelia Wilson 2 Oct 1814, daughter of Andrew and Amelia Glasgow; citing Ref 10 / 529, parish 573 / 1.</ref>
#[[Wilson-135260|Robert Glasgow Wilson]].<ref>Paisley High Church, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : accessed 30 Dec 2025), Robert Glasgow Wilson 17 Jul 1817, son of Andrew and Amelia Glasgow; citing Ref 10 / 562, parish 573 / 1.</ref>
Following their marriage, Andrew and Amelia moved to Paisley, Renfrewshire, where their children were born and Andrew was employed as a Merchant. They later moved to Ardrossan, Ayrshire, where Andrew passed away on 31 August 1830.<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Death and Burials," database with images, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : viewed 30 Dec 2025), death of Andrew Wilson, 31 Aug 1830; citing Ref No: 20 / 282, parish 596: 31 Aug 1830 Died at Ardrossan Andrew Wilson portioner of Wallast in this parish.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Andrew was described in a contemporary account as "sometimes daft, and one time he attempted to cut his throat."<ref>Andro Crawfurd, Cairn of Lochwinyoch matters: colleckit betwix 1827 and 1837.</ref>
